name: flutter-intercept
description: Inspect, pause, edit, block and mock your Flutter app's HTTP traffic — no code in your app, no setup. Just press F5.

flutterIntercept.enabled.description: Route the HTTP traffic of Dart/Flutter debug sessions through Flutter Intercept. When off, debug sessions are launched untouched.

flutterIntercept.port.description: Port of the local intercepting proxy. If it is busy the next free port (up to 8999) is used.

flutterIntercept.captureSource.description: Record where in your code each request was made (a stack trace sent out of band to the proxy), so you can jump from a request to its source line. Takes effect on the next launch. Flutter sessions only (plain Dart programs always record).

flutterIntercept.contractCheck.description: Check JSON responses against your json_serializable / freezed models (their generated *.g.dart) and show fields that would make fromJson throw, such as a null in a non-nullable field.

flutterIntercept.rewriteLocalhost.description: Send requests the app makes to the emulator host aliases (10.0.2.2, 10.0.3.2) to this machine's localhost. localhost and 127.0.0.1 already reach this machine through the proxy. Never applies to physical iPhones (LAN mode).

enumDescriptions: AI agents can read traffic and add mocks/blocks/breakpoints (every change is confirmed by the agent client).
AI agents can only read traffic.
flutterIntercept.agent.access.description: What AI agents (Copilot agent mode, Claude Code, Cursor, other MCP clients) may do.

flutterIntercept.agent.redactSecrets.description: Hide Authorization, cookies, API keys, tokens and passwords from AI agents (tool results and HAR exports). The app always receives the real values.

flutterIntercept.agent.mcpPort.description: Port of the local MCP server for AI agents (listens on 127.0.0.1 only). If it is busy, the next free port is used.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_status
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show proxy, session and traffic status.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get Flutter Intercept status: whether the intercepting proxy runs, the running debug sessions (device, program), how many requests are recorded and paused, and the agent access level. Call this first to see whether an app is running before using the other tools.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_list_requests
languageModelTools.userDescription: List recorded HTTP requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List HTTP requests the running Flutter/Dart app made (newest first), recorded by Flutter Intercept's proxy. Filter by URL glob (* matches any characters), method, status (code, class like "4xx", or "error"), state or start time. Returns ids; call get_request for headers and bodies. Secrets are redacted.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

status.description: An exact status code, a class ("2xx".."5xx"), or "error" (failed/aborted exchanges).

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_request
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Get HTTP request details
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show one request with headers and bodies.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get one recorded HTTP exchange by id: method, URL, status, request/response headers and decoded bodies (long bodies truncated, binary bodies summarised, secrets redacted), timings and error. Use after list_requests or wait_for_request. Pass snippet ("curl", "dart_http" or "dio") to also get the request as runnable code (redacted values stay "[redacted]"). For large JSON responses prefer get_body_shape first.

maxBodyChars.description: Bodies longer than this are cut and marked truncated.

snippet.description: Also return the request as code: "curl", "dart_http" (package:http) or "dio". Built from the redacted view.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_wait_for_request
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Wait for an HTTP request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Wait for a matching request to complete.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Wait until the app makes a request matching a URL glob (and optional method/status) and it completes, then return it. Use this right after triggering an action to verify the resulting network call. After hot_restart or launch_app you can call wait_for_request directly: requests sent since the restart/launch are included, even if they finished before this call. Otherwise only requests starting after this call count (pass sinceMs to choose). Returns the sinceMs it used, and {timedOut: true} after timeoutMs (default 30 s, max 120 s).

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

status.description: An exact status code, a class ("2xx".."5xx"), or "error" (failed/aborted exchanges).

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch ms), or "now" = when this call starts. Default: the start of the latest launch_app/hot_restart if it was within the last 120 s (so requests the app sent since then count), otherwise "now".

anyOf.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

timeoutMs.description: Give up after this long (max 120000) and return {timedOut: true}.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_list_paused
languageModelTools.userDescription: List requests paused at a breakpoint.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List exchanges currently paused by a breakpoint rule, with their phase (request or response) and the time they auto-resume. Resume or abort them with resume_request / abort_request.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_list_rules
languageModelTools.userDescription: List mock, block and breakpoint rules.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: List the active intercept rules (mocks, blocks, breakpoints) in priority order: the first enabled matching rule wins. Rules created by agents are named "[agent] ...".

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_export_har
languageModelTools.userDescription: Export recorded traffic to a HAR file.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Export recorded exchanges (optionally filtered by URL, method, start time) as a HAR 1.2 file under the project's .dart_tool/flutter_intercept/exports/ and return its path. Secrets are redacted according to the user's setting.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_request_source
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Find the code that sent a request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show the Dart call site that sent a request.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Find where in the app's Dart code a recorded request was made. Returns appFrame (the app's call site: function, package URI, path relative to the project, line, column) and the stack frames (inProject marks the project's own files; afterAsyncGap marks frames after an await). Use it to go from an unexpected, failing or duplicated request straight to the code that sent it. Returns {available: false, reason} when there is no trace: source capture off, a request sent by the editor/an agent, or the trace has not arrived yet (retry shortly).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_get_body_shape
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Get JSON body structure
languageModelTools.userDescription: Show the structure of a JSON body.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Get the structure of a recorded JSON response (or request, which:"request") body without its values: key names and types only, every array merged into one element shape plus its length. Compact even for megabyte bodies, so use it before get_request to understand an API response or to write/fix model classes and parsing code. Notation: "string" | "integer" | "number" | "boolean" | "null"; unions like "string|null"; "key?" = missing in some merged objects; arrays {"[]": element shape, "length": n or "min-max"}; {"|": [...]} = a union mixing objects/arrays; "{…}" / "[…]" = deeper than maxDepth; "…" = more keys omitted. Non-JSON bodies return {shape: null, reason}.

maxDepth.description: Nesting depth to describe (1-12); deeper structure shows as "{…}" / "[…]".

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_check_contract
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Check responses against the Dart models
languageModelTools.userDescription: Check JSON responses against the Dart models.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check recorded JSON responses against the app's own Dart models — exactly what the generated fromJson (json_serializable / freezed *.g.dart) would do with them. Finds the fields that would make parsing throw (error: a null or missing non-nullable field, a string where an int is expected, an unknown enum value) or are suspicious (warning). Pass id for one exchange, or url/method/sinceMs for the latest matching ones; model forces a model class. Each result says which model was used and how it was found (via: retrofit/chopper annotations, the request's stack trace, or the user's choice), or checked:false with the reason (no model mapped, not JSON, …). Violations give the JSON path, the model field, expected vs actual type and the model file:line (project-relative). Use it when the app shows a parse error ("type 'Null' is not a subtype of type 'String'") or after changing a model.

id.description: Check this one exchange. Omit to check the latest matching JSON responses.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only exchanges that started at or after this time (epoch milliseconds).

model.description: Check against this Dart model class (e.g. "User") instead of the one found automatically.

limit.description: Max exchanges to check when no id is given (newest first), 1-50.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_generate_model
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Generate Dart models from traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Generate Dart models from recorded responses.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Generate Dart model classes from the app's recorded JSON responses: every recorded sample of the same method + route is merged (a field missing in some samples becomes optional, a field seen null becomes nullable, int+double becomes double), nested objects get their own classes. Style follows the project (freezed, json_serializable or plain fromJson/toJson) unless style is given. Returns {files: [{path, content}], samples, route}: nothing is written, so write the files yourself (paths are suggestions relative to the project) and run build_runner for freezed/json_serializable. Secret field values are redacted before inference. Make the app call the endpoint a few times with different data first for better nullability.

id.description: A recorded exchange; every recorded response of the same method + route (e.g. GET /users/{id}) is used as a sample.

url.description: Or: the newest matching JSON response picks the route; all its recorded samples are used.

name.description: Root class name (default: from the URL, e.g. "User" for /users/{id}).

style.description: Code style. Default: the project's own (freezed > json_serializable > plain, from pubspec.yaml).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_generate_fixture_test
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Generate a fixture test from traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Generate JSON fixtures and a test from recorded requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Turn recorded exchanges into a test: one JSON fixture file per response under test/fixtures/ plus a test file that serves them with the project's mocking library (http_mock_adapter for Dio, package:http's MockClient, or mocktail for a Retrofit interface). Pass ids or a url glob. Returns {files: [{path, content}]} without writing them; adjust the generated test to call your repository/service and assert what matters. Always built from the redacted view: secrets appear as "[redacted]".

ids.description: Recorded exchanges to turn into fixtures (1-20).

url.description: Or: the newest (up to 20) finished exchanges matching this URL.

style.description: Test style. Default: the project's own dev_dependencies (http_mock_adapter > mocktail > mock_client).

name.description: snake_case base name for the files (default: from the first request, e.g. "get_user").

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_assert_traffic
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Assert on recorded traffic
languageModelTools.userDescription: Check that expected requests and responses happened.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Check in one call that the app made the expected requests: matching url (glob; * matches any characters) and method since sinceMs (default: the latest launch_app/hot_restart, else all recorded traffic), with expect: status (code, "2xx".., "error"), count {min, max, exact} (default: at least one), order (URL globs requested in that order), json assertions on every matched response ({path: "$.items[0].id", exists | equals | type}), maxDurationMs. withinMs waits (event-driven, max 120 s) for the requests to arrive; it never hangs. Returns {pass, matched, ids, failures: [readable reasons]}. Failure texts name the request, path and expectation but never echo response values; equals compares with the redacted view (a secret only equals "[redacted]"). Use it as the final check of a change instead of reading bodies by hand.

url.description: Requests to check: a glob on the full URL; * matches any characters.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

sinceMs.description: Only requests that started at or after this time (epoch ms). Default: the start of the latest launch_app/hot_restart if within the last 120 s, otherwise all recorded traffic.

withinMs.description: Wait up to this long (max 120000) for the expected requests. 0 = check what is recorded now. With count.max or count.exact the whole window is observed.

status.description: Every matched request has this status: a code, a class ("2xx".."5xx") or "error".

count.description: How many matching requests. Default: at least one.

order.description: URL globs that must have been requested in this order (each one starting after the previous one), among all requests since sinceMs.

items.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

path.description: JSON path into the response body: "$.user.avatar_url", "$.items[0].id", "$.items[*].price" ([*] = every element), "$['odd key']". No filters or "..".

exists.description: true: the path selects at least one value; false: it selects nothing. Default true when neither equals nor type is given.

equals.description: Every selected value deep-equals this JSON value. Compared with what get_request shows: a secret field only equals "[redacted]".

type.description: Every selected value has this JSON type ("integer" = a whole number).

items.description: An assertion on the JSON response body of every matched request.

maxDurationMs.description: Every matched request finished within this many ms.

expect.description: What must hold. Every given expectation is checked.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_mock
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that answers matching requests with a fake response.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Make the app receive a fake response for matching requests (the real server is not contacted). Use it to test error states and edge cases (e.g. status 500, empty lists, slow responses via delayMs) without touching the backend. The rule is inserted first so it wins. Pass times (e.g. 1 = only the next request, to test a retry) or ttlMs to have it removed automatically; otherwise remove it with remove_rule when done.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

headers.description: Response headers. content-type defaults to application/json when body is an object.

body.description: Response body: text, or a JSON object/array (sent as JSON).

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_block
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that blocks matching requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Block matching requests: answer with a status (default 403) or reset the connection (mode "reset") to simulate a network failure. Inserted first; times / ttlMs remove it automatically, otherwise remove it with remove_rule when done. For timeouts, slow or truncated responses use simulate_network.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_breakpoint
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that pauses matching requests or responses.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Pause matching requests before they are sent (phase "request") or their responses before the app gets them (phase "response", default). Paused exchanges appear in list_paused; continue them with resume_request (optionally edited) or abort_request. The app may time out if left paused. times: 1 pauses only the next matching request.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_remove_rule
languageModelTools.userDescription: Remove a rule.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Remove an intercept rule by id (see list_rules). Clean up the mocks, blocks and breakpoints you added once you are done.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_resume_request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Resume a paused request or response, optionally edited.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Resume a paused exchange, optionally editing it first: for a paused request method/url/headers/body, for a paused response status/headers/body. headers replaces the whole header set; omit body to keep it.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

body.description: New decoded body text. Omit to keep the original body.

edit.description: Changes to apply before resuming. Omit to resume unchanged.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_abort_request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Abort a paused request.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Abort a paused exchange: the app sees a connection reset.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_clear_requests
languageModelTools.userDescription: Clear the recorded traffic list.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Clear the recorded traffic list (in-flight and paused exchanges are kept). Useful before a step so that list_requests only shows what follows.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_launch_app
languageModelTools.userDescription: Launch the app in a debug session with interception.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Start the Flutter/Dart app in a normal VS Code debug session; Flutter Intercept routes its HTTP traffic through the proxy automatically. Optional deviceId (see get_status / the selected device), program (e.g. lib/main_dev.dart) and flutterMode (debug or profile). Returns {sessionId, sinceMs} once the session started; then call wait_for_request directly — requests the app sent since the launch are included.

deviceId.description: Flutter device id (e.g. "emulator-5554", a simulator UDID). Omit to use the device selected in VS Code.

program.description: Entry point, e.g. "lib/main_dev.dart". Omit for the default (lib/main.dart).

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_stop_app
languageModelTools.userDescription: Stop the app debug session(s).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Stop an intercepted debug session (or all of them when sessionId is omitted).

sessionId.description: Omit to stop every intercepted session.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_hot_restart
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Hot restart Flutter app
languageModelTools.userDescription: Hot restart the running app.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Hot-restart the running app (or all intercepted sessions) so it starts over with the current code and rules; interception stays on. Returns {restarted, sinceMs}. Then call wait_for_request directly to verify the network calls made at startup: requests sent since the restart are included, even ones that finished before wait_for_request was called.

sessionId.description: Omit to hot-restart every intercepted session.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_simulate_network
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Simulate network conditions (all app traffic or matching requests)
languageModelTools.userDescription: Throttle or break the network for the app or for matching requests.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Simulate bad network conditions to test loading states, timeouts, retries and offline handling. Without url: set the profile for ALL app traffic: "slow-3g", "fast-3g", "flaky" (20% of requests fail), "offline" (every request fails), "custom" (latencyMs, kbps, dropRate), or "none" to restore normal speed (do this when done). With url (a glob; * matches any characters): add a rule, inserted first, that slows only matching requests with the given profile, or makes them fail with fault ("reset", "timeout", "truncate", "dns"); times / ttlMs remove the rule automatically, otherwise use remove_rule. Mocks and blocks still answer instantly. get_status shows the active profile; affected exchanges carry a "simulated" label.

profile.description: "slow-3g" (+400 ms, 400 kbps), "fast-3g" (+150 ms, 1600 kbps), "flaky" (+200 ms, 20% of requests fail), "offline" (every request fails), "custom" (use latencyMs/kbps/dropRate), "none" (restore). Required unless `fault` is given.

latencyMs.description: custom: added latency per request, ms.

kbps.description: custom: response bandwidth, kilobits per second.

dropRate.description: custom: share of requests that fail (0-1).

url.description: Only affect requests matching this URL glob (adds a rule, inserted first). Omit to set the profile for ALL app traffic.

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

fault.description: With url: make matching requests fail instead of slowing them: "reset" (connection reset), "timeout" (no answer until the client gives up), "truncate" (response cut mid-body), "dns" (lookup failure).

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_resend_request
languageModelTools.userDescription: Send a recorded request again, optionally edited.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Send a recorded request again through the proxy, optionally edited (method, url, headers, body), without involving the app — e.g. to check a fix on the backend or try a different payload. Only for an app request that reached the real server unchanged (state "completed", no rule matched it, not from a physical device over LAN), and only to that request's own origin: edit.url may change path and query, never scheme, host or port. Anything else is refused with the reason. Omitted fields keep the original, including secret headers you only see as "[redacted]"; a "[redacted]" value in edit.headers (or the query) is replaced by the original. Rules and the network profile apply. Returns {id, sinceMs}: the new exchange starts "pending"; wait for it with wait_for_request (same url, that sinceMs) or check get_request(id).

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

url.description: Absolute http(s) URL with the SAME origin (scheme, host, port) as the recorded request; only path and query may change.

headers.description: Replaces the WHOLE header set. A value of "[redacted]" is replaced by the original value of that header.

body.description: New body text. Omit to keep the original body.

edit.description: Changes to the recorded request. Omit to send it unchanged.

languageModelTools.name: flutter_intercept_add_mutation
languageModelTools.displayName: Flutter Intercept: Add response mutation rule
languageModelTools.userDescription: Add a rule that changes fields of real JSON responses.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Let matching requests reach the real server, then change its JSON response before the app gets it: ops [{path: "$.user.avatar_url", op: "null"}, {path: "$.items[*].price", op: "set", value: "9.99"}, {path: "$.email", op: "delete"}]. For an exact number form use valueJson (JSON text written byte-exact) instead of value: "1.0" to send a double (an int-typed Dart field then throws), integers beyond 2^53. Use it to reproduce or test how the app handles a null/missing/mistyped field from the backend (e.g. "Null is not a subtype of String") without mocking the whole response. Non-JSON responses pass unchanged. The rule is inserted first; times (e.g. 1) or ttlMs remove it automatically, otherwise use remove_rule. Affected exchanges carry a "simulated" label; check_contract shows what the models make of them.

url.description: URL glob on the full URL; * matches any characters (e.g. "https://api.example.com/v1/users*", "*/users/*"). Matched against the URL as you see it (redacted query values read "[redacted]").

method.description: HTTP method (case-insensitive). Omit to match any method.

path.description: JSON path into the response body: "$.user.avatar_url", "$.items[0].id", "$.items[*].price" ([*] = every element), "$['odd key']". No filters or "..".

op.description: "null" sets the field to null, "delete" removes the key (or array element), "set" replaces it with `value`.

value.description: With op "set": the new JSON value, e.g. "42" to send a number as a string. Max 1 MB.

valueJson.description: With op "set", instead of value: the new value as JSON text, written byte-exact. Use it when the exact number form matters: "1.0" (a double, which Dart parses as double, not int), integers beyond 2^53 ("12345678901234567890"), "1e3". Wins over value.

items.description: One change to the JSON response body.

ops.description: Changes applied in order to the real JSON response (1-20).

times.description: Apply the rule to the first N matching requests only (1-1000); it is then removed automatically.

ttlMs.description: Remove the rule automatically after this many milliseconds (1000-86400000).

name.description: Optional label; it is shown as "[agent] <name>" in the rules list.

scripts.test:vsix: npm run build && npm run package && node build.mjs --tests && FI_VSIX=flutter-intercept.vsix node dist-test/runTest.js
